definitions.explanation: A group of things sharing common characteristics. Used as a standalone noun or as a suffix attached to other nouns to indicate a category or class.

examples.japanese: この{類|るい}の{本|ほん}が{好|す}きだ。
examples.english: I like this kind of book.

examples.japanese: {書類|しょるい}を{種類|しゅるい}ごとに{分|わ}けてください。
examples.english: Please sort the documents by type.

examples.japanese: {穀物|こくもつ}{類|るい}や{豆|まめ}{類|るい}は{栄養|えいよう}が{豊富|ほうふ}だ。
examples.english: Grains and legumes are rich in nutrients.

notes:
USAGE:
As a suffix, {類|るい} attaches to nouns to create category labels: {魚|さかな}{類|るい} (fish, as a category), {野菜|やさい}{類|るい} (vegetables), {肉|にく}{類|るい} (meats). This usage is common in menus, nutrition labels, and classification systems.

As a standalone noun, {類|るい} means "kind" or "sort": この{類|るい}の... (this type of...), {類|るい}を{見|み}ない (unparalleled).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {穀物|こくもつ}{類|るい} (grains)
- {魚介|ぎょかい}{類|るい} (seafood)
- {人類|じんるい} (humanity, humankind)
- {書類|しょるい} (documents)
- {類|るい}を{見|み}ない (unprecedented, unparalleled)
